analysis.evidence: In מִן הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא יָצָא, “from that land he went out,” מִן introduces the place of departure for יָצָא.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מִן הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא means “from that land.” The demonstrative points back to Shinar in verse 10, identifying the territory from which the departure took place.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes a common noun of both genders in the singular absolute. The feminine singular demonstrative הַהִוא agrees with the noun here.

analysis.evidence: In מִן הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא, “from that land,” הַהִוא follows הָאָרֶץ and agrees with it in gender, number, and definiteness. It points back to the land of Shinar in the preceding verse.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes the third-person feminine singular pronoun הִוא, the Pentateuchal spelling of הִיא. The pronoun functions as a demonstrative.

analysis.evidence: The phrase מִן הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא (‘from that land’) identifies the place of departure.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: go out, depart from a place or someone’s presence

analysis.evidence: The repeated direct-object marker אֶת introduces Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah as the cities he built.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular. יִּבֶן is the shortened form of בָּנָה.
Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The repeated object marker אֶת sets וְאֶת רְחֹבֹת עִיר between Nineveh and Calah in the list of cities built. רְחֹבֹת and the following עִיר together name one city.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with a feminine plural ending and no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Rehoboth, the first element of the place name Rehoboth-Ir

analysis.evidence: וְאֶת introduces רְחֹבֹת עִיר as one of the places built, between Nineveh and Calah. Within that name, עִיר supplies the sense “city” in “open places of a city.”
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun with no prefix or suffix. It completes the place-name רְחֹבֹת עִיר.
